pr_title: Fix dynamically add/remove WLED strip segments
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

WLED allows a user to split a single LED strip into multiple segments and control these separately.

Recent a recent update to WLED, it possible for the user to add/remove segments via the UI on the fly (before it was an API only feature).

With the release of WLED 0.10, users can just really easy click and change the segments from the web interface. This break HA.

This PR makes a start on fixing that. The tests aren't the prettiest, mainly because I've frozen the dataclass object on the package side. For a followup, I'm planning on unfreezing it and rewriting parts of the tests without mocking aiohttp.

issue_context.body:

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->

When I create a new segment in the WLED web interface, I notice that a new HA entity is created for that segment (`light.outdoor_leds_1`,`light.outdoor_leds_2`, etc).  When I delete the segment in the web interface, my HA logs start filling with messages like this:

```
2020-02-11 11:54:39 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.entity] Update for light.outdoor_leds_2 fails
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 279, in async_update_ha_state
    await self.async_device_update()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 459, in async_device_update
    await self.async_update()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/wled/__init__.py", line 195, in async_update
    await self._wled_update()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/wled/light.py", line 235, in _wled_update
    self._effect = self.wled.device.state.segments[self._segment].effect.name
IndexError: list index out of range
```


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue:  0.105.5
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):  Docker
- Integration causing this issue:  WLED
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/wled/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml

```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information

@frenck is aware of this issue, per a conversation I had with him on Discord.  He said:

Yep
HA doesn't know
On HA start, it will check for the current available devices
A restart is needed in that case
Would be nice to be able to handle that dynamically, that should be possible 
check the devices on each update
and that start to unload the entity, deregister the event listeners for updates and update the devices & entity registries
same for creation btw, which isn't dynamically at this point as well
comments: Hey there @frenck, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`wled`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L399) for? Thanks!

Yes, I was informed.
This integration is written on the earlier concepts of segments and needs to be adjusted to the current, new release, of WLED.

If I may add to the WLED segment issue, in the tests I ran the power and brightness controls work on all segments from any segment, ie switching/dimming a segment switches/dims the whole strip. I would expect the different segments to be controllable separately, since they show up as distinct entities. Color selection, however, works fine. Thanks for all the great work.
@dvdavide besides being off-topic for the issue, WLED simply doesn't provide controls for that on their API. Feel free to raise a request for that @ WLED itself.
I assume segment support is still an open issue. Just updated to WLED 0.10.0 and was going to look at my light config while still stuck at home.

review_comments: This can be done concurrently with asyncio.gather.
I fail to see how that works here. As gather has to be awaited, which I don't care about at this point. It just needs to fire the task and forget?
Sorry, I was reading one thing and thinking something else.
Do we need to change time from the last update? Ie add another scan interval to the previous fired event?
Not really, as it just fires the event again. Effectively, we are not changing the current time here, just faking the fired time.
Ok. I was thinking about the coordinator debouncer and if that would interfere with the second call.
Yes, that was my initial hunch as well. However, as the previous is blocked until done, the coordinator is free when we reach this point.
There's a default cooldown of 10 seconds. We're not blocking for that time, right?
Nevermind, the coordinator refresh on interval cancels the timer task of the debouncer. It's only `coordinator.async_request_refresh` that is debounced.
